A.explanation: Same proton number $x$ as Q but nucleon number $y-1$ is different, so same element with different neutron number.

B.explanation: Proton number is $x-1$ not $x$, so this is a different element, not an isotope of Q.

C.explanation: Proton number is $x+1$ not $x$, so this is a different element, not an isotope of Q.

D.explanation: Proton number is $x+1$ not $x$, so this cannot be an isotope even though the nucleon number is different.

hints: Notice the positions in $^{y}_{x}Q$: the lower number $x$ is the proton number $Z$ and the upper number $y$ is the nucleon number $A$.
Recall that isotopes of the same element have the same proton number $x$ but different numbers of neutrons, so $A = Z + N$ must change.
Compare each option to $^{y}_{x}Q$ and keep the lower number fixed at $x$ while looking for a different upper number.
walkthrough: Identify the notation in $^{y}_{x}Q$: lower $x$ is the proton number $Z$, upper $y$ is the nucleon number $A$, where $A = Z + N$.
State the isotope rule: isotopes are nuclei of the same element, so $Z$ must stay the same and $N$, hence $A$, must be different.
Check the lower numbers: only the nucleus with lower number $x$ can have the same proton number as Q.
Check the upper numbers: that nucleus has upper number $y-1$, which is different from $y$, meaning one fewer nucleon and therefore one fewer neutron.
Conclude that same $Z$ with different $A$ satisfies the isotope condition. This is option A.
